title: You Said the Word That Makes One Fall in Love...
text:
You said the word that makes one fall in love

To my ears. You have forgotten already. Well then.

Sleep peacefully. Your face must be serene

And beautiful at every hour.


When the seductive mouth enchants

It must be fresh, its speech pleasant;

For your trade of lover it is not good

The burning face of one who weeps much.


More glorious destinies claim you

Than that of carrying, between the black wells

Of dark circles, a mourning gaze.


Cover the ground with beautiful victims!

More harm to the world did the fatuous sword

Of some barbarous king — and he has a statue.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the bitter irony of the lover as a decorated conqueror.

title: You Who Will Never Be...
text:
Saturday it was, and caprice the kiss given,

caprice of a man, bold and fine,

but sweet was the masculine caprice

to this my heart, winged wolf cub.


It is not that I believe, I do not; if bent

over my hands I felt you divine

and I became drunk, I understand that this wine

is not for me, but I play and the die rolls...


I am that woman who lives alert;

you, the tremendous male who awakens

and is a torrent that widens into a river


and grows rougher as it runs and cuts.

Ah, I resist, but you have me entire,

you, who will never be wholly mine!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's alert resistance and its surrendering final turn.

title: One Day...
text:
You wander through those worlds as I do; do not tell me

you do not exist, you exist, we are to meet;

we shall not know each other, disguised and awkward

we shall set out along the roads.


We shall not know each other, distant one from another

you will feel my sighs and I will hear you sigh.

Where will the mouth be, the mouth that sighs?

We shall say, retracing the road.


Perhaps we will meet face to face someday,

perhaps we will manage to take off our disguises.

And now I ask myself... when it happens, if it happens,

will I know about sighs, will you know how to sigh?
editorial_note: The translation preserves the doubled uncertainty of recognition and sighing.

title: The Plea
text:
Lord, Lord, long ago, one day

I dreamed a love as no one ever could

dream it, some love that would be

all of life, all of poetry.


And winter passed and it did not come,

and spring also passed,

and summer persisted again,

and autumn found me with my waiting.


Lord, Lord; my back is bare,

make burst there, with rough hand,

the whip that bloodies the perverse!


For evening is already upon my life,

and this ardent and measureless passion

I have lost, Lord, making verses!




Languor, 1920
editorial_note: The translation keeps the final bitter claim that poetry itself consumed the passion.

title: Subconsciousness
text:
You have spoken, you have spoken and I have fallen asleep.

But I sleep and do not sleep, because I feel

that I am under supreme thought:

I live, I shall always live and I have lived.


You have spoken, you have spoken and I have fallen

into a stupor... even breath gives way.

Long ago, in the shadows, I have lost myself:

I am blind. I have no feeling.


Like space I am, like the void.

My whole body is a shadow

and I can rise like smoke:


I hear ethereal breaths... superhuman...

Fasten me to the earth with your hands,

for if the wind moves it must carry me away.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the trance-like repetition and the danger of becoming smoke.

title: For Ten Cents I Bought It on the Corner...
text:
For ten cents I bought it on the corner

and an ungainly angel sold it to me;

when I set about sharpening it

I saw it as a small and sturdy cannon.


The lead sprang out exploding ideas

and again the sad angel sharpened it.

I went out with it and a face of high bronze

hauled it from my memory. Distracted


I tossed it in my bag among handkerchiefs, letters,

dried flowers, coloring tubes,

bills, slips and nougats.


I was going I don't know where and violently

some vehicle lifted me, and my bag

kept knocking with its bomb inside.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the pencil as both writing tool and explosive device.

title: The Divine Love
text:
I go looking for you, love that never arrives;

I go looking for you, love that withholds yourself.

I sharpen myself to know if you guess me;

I bend myself to know if you surrender to me.


My storms, wandering,

have quieted on a bundle of thorns;

my flesh bleeds purplish drops

because when I would save you, oh child, you refuse me.


Look, I am standing on the logs,

sometimes a few dreams are enough

to light the flame that ruins me


Save me, love, and with your pure hands

change this fire into limpid sweetnesses

and make of my logs a green branch.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the prayer-like demand for love to transform fire into green life.

title: Love
text:
From heaven descends the devilish point

with which you wound and deceive mortal flesh.

Anointed it comes with divine tricks

and heaven and earth join its poison.


The blood of man that starts in the wound

blooms into forests: its grown canes

of golden shadows split the entrails

of the dark sky, and their ascent asks.


In their vain waiting for the answer

the canes bend their steep heads.

The sky flames its blue gauzes.


Black winds, behind the crystals

of the stars, move great handles

of dead worlds, through their outskirts.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the cosmic violence of love as wound, poison, and moving dead worlds.

title: The Clamor
text:
Once, walking through life,

out of pity, out of love,

as a fountain gives, without reserve,

I gave my heart.


And I said to the passerby, without malice,

and perhaps with fervor:

-I obey the law that governs us:

I have given my heart.


And as soon as I said it, like an echo

the voice had already spread:

-See that bad woman passing:

She has given her heart.


From mouth to mouth, over rooftops,

this clamor rolled:

-Throw stones, hey, at her face;

she has given her heart!


My face is already bleeding, yes,

but not from shame,

for I turn to men and repeat:

I have given my heart!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the public accusation and the speaker's unashamed refrain.

title: Beneath Your Gazes
text:
It is beneath your gazes where I never founder;

it is beneath your tranquil gazes where I gain

properties of water; where I laugh, talkative,

covering myself with flowers like the vine.


It is beneath your blue gazes where I am more than enough

for grief; I awaken new dreams and act

with such hopes, that it seems Spring

had dictated to me an exquisite desire:


To have the soul fresh, clean; to be like linen

that is white and smells of herbs. To possess the divine

secret of laughter; that the vermilion mouth


persist until the last silence, beautiful, strong,

and sip in the supreme corolla of Death

with its last bee!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the water-and-flower transformation under the beloved's gaze.
